FA 101.name: Basic Design I
FA 101.description: Basic design concepts: form, pattern, composition, theme, organization, color, texture. Introduction to design problem solving skills. Abstract 2D and 3D design problems.

FA 102.name: Basic Design II
FA 102.description: Continuation of basic design concepts: space, proportion, scale, human dimensions and activities. 3D design problems: user, function, structure.

FA 103.name: Drawing I
FA 103.description: Exploration of the human figure, its parts and its form as far as structure and functions are concerned. Drawing fundamentals in figurative expression, proportions and compositional expressions by working directly from the model in various media.

FA 104.name: Drawing II
FA 104.description: Exploration of visual form, character and gesture of movements of the human figure. Searching, evaluating and applying the basic elements of life drawing: line, form, color, value, module and composition.

FA 105.name: Foundation Studio I
FA 105.description: Introduction to the basic elements and the principles of two-dimensional design. Development of an understanding of the visual language while improving abilities in abstract thinking and problem solving.

FA 106.name: Foundation Studio II
FA 106.description: As a continuation of FA 105, new subjects such as color, value, texture, transparency and layers via basic 2D, 3D and 4D design problems.

FA 107.name: Drawing and Visual Expressions
FA 107.description: Improvement of drawing skills by means of discovering the ways of how to look and what to see in the environment in which we live.

FA 131.name: Technical Drawing
FA 131.description: An introduction to drafting techniques, tools and materials. Multiview drawings: top, front and side views. Paraline drawings: axonometric and oblique projection. Perspective drawings: one-point and two point perspective projection. Initiation of CAD drawings of simple solid forms.

FA 132.name: Design Graphics
FA 132.description: An overview of the relationship between design and drawing. Introduction to architectural orthographic drawings: plan, section and elevation. 3D drawing and rendering techniques: one-point and two point interior perspectives; cut-away paraline drawings. Board presentation techniques. Initiation of CAD drawings of floor plans, sections and elevations.

FA 171.name: Introduction to Art, Design and Culture I
FA 171.description: This undergraduate core course examines a diverse range of approaches to visual culture. Through lectures, class discussions and audio-visual media, this course introduces students to key theories and concepts on art, design and architecture. During the course, the students will develop an understanding of historical, social and political knowledge that regulate the production and consumption of visual culture. The students will be evaluated based on class participation, assignments, quizzes, oral presentation, a midterm and a final exam.

FA 172.name: Introduction to Art, Design and Culture II
FA 172.description: This undergraduate course is part of the two-semester course (FA 171 and FA 172) which aims to develop a historical and critical knowledge on artistic and cultural production, focusing on the social function of art, modernism, post-modernism, the art institutions, and media studies. During the course, the students will develop an awareness of the visual environment in a theoretical and practical way by applying the concepts given in the lectures and the readings to visual material.

FA 201.name: Art Studio I
FA 201.description: Introduction to the art elements, arts techniques. For the students who are prepared to focus on developing a personal point of view in art.

FA 202.name: Art Studio II
FA 202.description: A continuation of FA 201. Development of concepts towards the transformation of basic design criteria to artwork with contribution of fantasy and imagination.

FA 203.name: Drawing III
FA 203.description: Study of the figure to improve drawing skills and knowledge. Fast sketching, figural expression, transformation, drawing materials and techniques.

FA 204.name: Drawing IV
FA 204.description: Examining the human body in terms of form, color and color values. Studies leading to individual expression in model drawing based on the basic principles of art.

FA 207.name: Artistic Anatomy
FA 207.description: A course for those who wish to gain the ability to catch the perfection of human body form by creating techniques and attitudes in observing and drawing the skeleton and live models.

FA 208.name: Anatomical Figure Drawing
FA 208.description: Furthering of the Artistic and Anatomical approach to figure drawing by critical interpretation and detailed study of the works of Renaissance Great Masters by means of studio sessions.

FA 211.name: Introduction to Painting I
FA 211.description: Building basic technical skills. Experiments with the use of paint. Conceptual and practical experiments on color mixing. Examining the creative processes through these experiments. (non-FA majors only).

FA 212.name: Introduction to Painting II
FA 212.description: Research on visual elements; form-color, structure, volume and composition. Relations between light, color and sight. Developing the skill of design, compositional capacity through working on certain projects. (non-FA majors only).

FA 213.name: Introduction to Printmaking I
FA 213.description: Introduction to the fundamental techniques of water-based silkscreen printmaking. Manual and digital processes. Independent work and application of processes in creative ways while mastering the applied techniques. All projects in small editions while the final project involving a multi-process, multi-layer edition. Individual and group critiques throughout the semester.

FA 214.name: Introduction to Printmaking II
FA 214.description: Introduction to the fundamental techniques of oil-based intaglio printmaking. Traditional and contemporary applications and experimentation. Working independently on monoprints, small editions, and a multi-layer, multi-plate final project. Individual and group critiques throughout the semester.

FA 215.name: Introduction to Sculpture I
FA 215.description: An introductory studio course on the basic concepts, materials and processes of sculpture, with an emphasis on the understanding of perception and representation of three dimensional objects for students from other disciplines. (non-FA majors only.)

FA 217.name: Introduction to Ceramics I
FA 217.description: Introduction to the basic material and techniques in ceramics including design, glazing, firing, loading and unloading kiln. Practice of what has been studied based on an artist's life and work. By the end of the course, writing of a research paper demonstrating knowledge of design, glazing and firing based on the artist chosen to work on.

FA 219.name: Ancient Techniques and New Technology in Mosaic
FA 219.description: An experimental course, combining the current techniques and the new technology in ceramics such as using ceramic colors on fired tiles. Search for new ways of expression in color. Using the clay as the canvas.

FA 223.name: Visual Perception in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
FA 223.description: Examination of subjects such as psychology of visual perception, seeing the color and perception of color-form, concepts and theories of color.

FA 262.name: Fine Arts Seminar
FA 262.description: Critical assessment of selected national and international artist's works and their ideas and approaches.

FA 271.name: History of Art
FA 271.description: A chronological survey of the history of art from the Stone Age to the Byzantine World.

FA 272.name: History of Art II
FA 272.description: A chronological survey of the history of art from the Renaissance period to the 21. Cent.

FA 290.name: Summer Practice I
FA 290.description: Minimum 6 weeks practice at arts-related institutions.

FA 301.name: Art Studio III
FA 301.description: A studio class in one of the selected fields of fine arts based on independent project work. The ceramics section applying underlying principles of sketching and critiquing. As one of the requirements of the course, individual or group tutorials during project work. By the end of the course, completion and presentation of three pieces of project based on course objectives.

FA 302.name: Art Studio IV
FA 302.description: Continuation of FA 301. With emphasis on the development of individual vision and personal expression.

FA 304.name: Special Problems in Drawing
FA 304.description: Studies of the human body concerning form, color and value. Exploration of individual expression by using models to build up thought and imagery. Contemporary figural expressions.

FA 321.name: Computers in Art
FA 321.description: Practical digital art skills with critical analysis of contemporary issues like AI tools, NFTs, digital ethics, and glitch aesthetics. Recent transformations in technology, artistic creation, ownership, and audience engagement.

FA 322.name: Generative Art, Design and Concepts
FA 322.description: Digital art through hands-on practice and critical analysis. Technical skills in image manipulation, AI tools, and interactive systems along with contemporary issues like NFTs, digital ethics, and glitch aesthetics.

FA 331.name: Creative Artificial Intelligence: Technology and Artistry
FA 331.description: Introduction to technical materials used in various visual arts and technical, physical and chemical characteristics of the natural and synthetic materials used in sculpture, painting, printmaking and ceramics.

FA 332.name: Art,Technology and Science
FA 332.description: Art has been deeply interconnected with changes in technology, it has either responded to it or has changed with it leading to redefinitions in the making of art as well as changes in how it is viewed. This course examines symptomatic positions of interaction in the history, and discusses the contemporary situation with emphasis on recent changes.

FA 361.name: Philosophy of Art I
FA 361.description: Philosophical issues that arise concerning the creation, interpretation and viewing of art, since Plato. What is "mimesis"; who is the best judge of art; is art beautiful and good; should art be viewed dis-interestedly.

FA 390.name: Summer Practice II
FA 390.description: Minimum 6 weeks practice at arts-related institutions.

FA 401.name: Art Studio V
FA 401.description: Studio work related to the student's preference of thematic possibilities in the selected field of fine arts.

FA 402.name: Art Studio VI - Degree Project
FA 402.description: Individual studio work aiming to realize a coherent body of artwork in the selected field of fine arts.

FA 421.name: Analysis of Artwork
FA 421.description: Introduction to critical analysis of works of art by concentrating on the theoretical debates developed around various issues on art theory since the 19th century.

FA 422.name: Analysis of Art Work II
FA 422.description: Having dealt with the nature of painting, photography and cinema in the first part of this course, study of various postmodern approaches to art-such as semiotic, psychoanalytic, social and political approaches in order to foreground the impact of the postmodern theory on arts.

FA 462.name: Senior Seminar
FA 462.description: Working and assessment on selected contemporary issues of art, finding interdisciplinary and alternative ways of communication with public.

FA 465.name: Writing in Visual Arts
FA 465.description: A follow-up of the '"Research Methods'". Students conduct research and experiment in writing critical and historical essays on art. The essays are analyzed in class and the students are familiarized with signs, methods and techniques of editing and editorial practice.

FA 467.name: Curatorial Studies I
FA 467.description: An introduction to the study of museum education and curatorship, focusing on historical development of art institutions and society discussions.

FA 471.name: Special Issues in Contemporary Art I
FA 471.description: This course examines international contemporary art through theoretical, political, and social lenses. Students explore how artists, critics, and curators address identity, globalization, digital culture, activism, and cultural representation.

FA 473.name: Contemporary Turkish Art
FA 473.description: Analysis of the general features of various movements in Modern Turkish Art. Painting, sculpture and ceramics in Turkey from the late nineteenth century to the present. Its evaluation in comparison with European and other modern art movements.
